profile.what: India's second-largest lead-acid battery maker (brand Amaron; also PowerZone, Quanta): automotive batteries for 2W/3W/4W/CV OEMs and the replacement market, home-energy (tubular/inverter batteries, home UPS), industrial batteries (telecom, UPS and data centres, railways, power control, solar), exports to 70+ countries, and Amaron Hi-Life lubricants. A New Energy business (lithium-ion packs for telecom, 2W/3W; chargers; a cell giga-factory and a 10 GWh BESS plant under construction in Telangana) sits in the 100% subsidiary ARACT.
profile.plants: 15 manufacturing facilities; ~70 mn units a year of automotive capacity and ~2.4 bn Ah industrial (Tirupati and Chittoor, Andhra Pradesh); ~1.8 mn tubular batteries (Chittoor); lead recycling at Cheyyar, Tamil Nadu (ARCSPL; 100,000 tonnes a year refining, to 150,000); pack plants 1.5 GWh mobility + 1.2 GWh stationary (Divitipally, Telangana) (Q1FY27 deck).
profile.reach: 1,500+ direct partners, 1,00,000+ points of sale; exports ~12% of standalone revenue (Rs1,652.7 cr outside India in FY26, AR FY26 note 22); market share in telecom (lead + lithium) >60% (Q1FY27 call).

aract.plan: Giga Cell plant at Divitipally: phase 1 = 2 GWh NMC (cylindrical 2170 cells), equipment due in Q3FY27, operations from Q2-CY2027 (commercialisation in H1FY28); 16 GWh by FY30 was the original plan (Rs9,500 cr over ~10 years) and is now 'a long-term ambition' to be calibrated to demand, with ESS (LFP) cells possibly prioritised. Customer Qualification Plant inaugurated 15-Jul-2026; E-Positive research lab to start in Q2FY27. 10 GWh BESS assembly plant (LFP, imported 314 Ah cells): initial capex Rs250-300 cr, operations in Q3FY27, ~5 GWh utilisation within 6-7 months, operating margin 5-6% at first, 7-8% with localisation. Pack business: telecom and 3W/2W packs, revenue Rs809 cr in FY26 (NEB segment), Rs209 cr in Q1FY27 (+70%).
aract.funding: Initial risk capital agreed ~Rs2,500 cr to complete five facilities (cell plant phase 1, CQP, E-Positive lab, BESS, packs); later capacity to be funded by the holding company and/or other options; Rs700-800 cr a year of post-tax, post-dividend cash generation at the parent (Q1FY27 call). FY27 group capex ~Rs1,700 cr, of which ~Rs1,300 cr New Energy; Rs450 cr spent in Q1 (Q1FY27 call).
aract.technology: Gotion (China) technology partnership did not go through (ICICI Direct, Jun-2026; Q1FY27 call); NMC cell technology taken in earlier and improved in-house; no broad Chinese tie-up possible given geopolitical restrictions; cathode materials from China. Cost gap vs Chinese cells 15-20% (Q1FY27 call). Cell R&D spend Rs100-150 cr in FY27.
aract.returns: At 8-10 GWh scale EBITDA margin 10-11% and ROCE 'low double digit' (CFO, Q4FY26 call).

q1fy27.volumes: Lead-acid revenue +22%; 4W and 2W aftermarket volume ~+15%; OEM 4W +24%, 2W +35%+; home energy (tubular and home UPS) +60%; tubular plant at 100% and trading ~15% of lead-acid revenue; automotive exports −20% (Middle East shipping); industrial lead-acid +2% (UPS volume +10%, telecom lead-acid down); lithium telecom volume +50%; New Energy revenue Rs209 cr (+70%+).
q1fy27.margin: Margin 10.1% (−140bp YoY): ~0.9pp from strategic spending (brand/IPL, Amaron Assist pilot, Factory of the Future debottlenecking expensed), plus alloy, sulphuric acid and plastics costs, warranty provisions on higher product costs, freight; ~3% price increase in June and a further 2-3% in August.
q1fy27.src: Q1FY27 presentation (10-Aug-2026) and call (11-Aug-2026); MOFSL and 360 ONE result notes (11-Aug-2026) for standalone lines; Screener.in (standalone and consolidated)

guidance: Lead-acid medium-term growth: 'anywhere between 9% to 10%' for the industry as a whole, mainly volume; prices extra, passed on with a lag in B2C and later in B2B (Q1FY27 call). MOFSL reports management's 'high single digit to low double digit'.
Margin: aim to reach 13-14% EBITDA margin at a ~Rs2 lakh/tonne lead base, timing uncertain; strategic spending to normalise over the next couple of quarters (Q4FY26 and Q1FY27 calls).
Capex FY27: ~Rs1,700 cr group, ~Rs1,300 cr New Energy, ~Rs400 cr lead-acid incl. recycling; Rs450 cr spent in Q1 (Q1FY27 call).
Lithium: Giga cell phase 1 (2 GWh NMC) from Q2-CY2027; BESS 10 GWh from Q3FY27; ~Rs2,500 cr initial risk capital for New Energy, further funding options open (Q1FY27 call).
Trading: share of traded batteries to fall as the tubular plant meets demand; lithium pack trading moves fully to ARACT from Q2FY27 (Q1FY27 call).
history: Amara Raja Batteries incorporated in Andhra Pradesh (CIN L31402AP1985PLC005305); listed on BSE (500008) and NSE
FY20

Promoter holding falls from 52.06% to 28.06% (Screener shareholding): the 24% held by Clarios (formerly Johnson Controls' battery arm) is no longer counted as promoter; Clarios later sold 10% + 14% = 24%

Andhra Pradesh Pollution Control Board issues a closure order against the company; the company challenged it in the AP High Court; the order was revoked on 18-Jul-2026 and the writ petition withdrawn (Q1FY27 call)
Clarios (ex-Johnson Controls Power Solutions) sells 10% for Rs1,276 cr (block deal)
New Energy plan: Rs9,500 cr 'Giga Corridor' in Telangana (16 GWh cells, 5 GWh packs by ~FY30); ARCSPL (recycling) and ARACT (lithium) incorporated (Jun- and Nov-2022)
Fire at the Chittoor tubular plant; net exceptional charge Rs47.65 cr in FY23; insurance received FY25 (Rs111 cr) and FY26 (Rs303 cr)
New Energy business transferred from the company to ARACT by slump sale (Rs223.96 cr)
Clarios sells its remaining 14% (~Rs1,561 cr) and exits
Renamed Amara Raja Energy & Mobility Ltd (from Amara Raja Batteries Ltd); ARPSL (power systems, chargers) acquired 29-Sep-2023 for Rs133 cr

NCLT sanctions demerger of Mangal Industries' plastic-components business into the company (appointed date 1-Apr-2022): 1.22 cr shares (Rs672.6 cr) to Mangal's holders; promoter stake 28.06% → 32.86%; goodwill Rs428 cr
FY25
Lead recycling plant at Cheyyar, Tamil Nadu (ARCSPL) starts operations
Customer Qualification Plant (lithium cells) inaugurated; Rs1,900 cr invested in ARACT by Aug-2026
